title: The lead corpus assumes a Flowable gap that Flowable closed in December 2025
content:
The lead corpus asserts, across 38 notes and one MoC, that "Flowable orchestrates WHEN things happen - the process/case instance is a mutable row and history is purgeable", and treats that as an open slot.

Primary-source research confirms the OSS half more strongly than the workbook did: the engine's own MyBatis mapper issues `update ${prefix}ACT_HI_PROCINST` with `START_TIME_` assignable, so mutability is quotable from source.

But two findings contradict the corpus. Flowable Enterprise shipped a business audit trail on 2025-12-16 whose records are documented as immutable, and it is procurable on-premise from a Swiss vendor with a Berlin office under ISO 27001 - so no sovereignty exclusion remains. Separately, "purgeable" overstates the default: automatic cleanup is disabled by default and retention is effectively infinite.

Both claims came from a lead workbook, not from primary sources. The resolution is scoping rather than deletion: the OSS finding stands when explicitly bounded to the Apache-2.0 edition, and the commercial pitch has to change from "Flowable cannot do this" to a price-and-features argument against an incumbent with 600+ enterprise customers. Unresolved: whether anyone wants to make that argument.
resolution: Resolved in favour of the primary sources. The workbook premise is true only of the Apache-2.0 edition, and the note that carried it now says so: the engine's own mapper proves mutability in OSS, Flowable Enterprise shipped an immutable business audit trail on 2025-12-16 that is procurable on-premise in the EU, and "purgeable" overstates a default in which cleanup is disabled. The 38 lead notes' seam is unchanged for an OSS deployment; what changed is the commercial argument, which is now an open question on the Leads running Flowable map rather than an unresolved contradiction.
description: 38 lead notes and a MoC are premised on Flowable lacking an immutable business audit trail. Primary sources show Enterprise shipped one on 2025-12-16, deployable on-premise in the EU.
